variants.headline: Party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}.
variants.body:
The leader of {party}, {leader}, has blundered in an election debate. The misstep is established, but the words involved and their effect on voters are not supplied here. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the debate event from a fabricated quotation or a claim that the election's outcome has been decided.

The gazette records the debate blunder without reproducing words not supplied to this notice. The gazette records the development as a matter deserving careful attention in the public interest.

variants.headline: A debate brings a leader's misstep
variants.sub: The party leader {leader}, of {party}, has made a debate misstep.
variants.body:
An election debate has included a blunder by {leader}, leader of {party}. Public speaking is part of political leadership, though an awkward moment is not a complete political record. For {target}, the question is judgment under scrutiny, without inventing what was said or how the audience responded to the mistake.

The gazette records the debate blunder without reproducing words not supplied to this notice. The gazette records the development as a matter deserving careful attention in the public interest.

variants.headline: Election argument meets an awkward moment
variants.sub: The leader of {party}, {leader}, has blundered in an election debate.
variants.body:
The party leader {leader}, of {party}, has made a debate misstep. It is legitimate political news, not a substitute for the whole contest. An assessment of {target} should keep the misstep in proportion and leave polling changes or electoral consequences outside the factual account.

The gazette records the debate blunder without reproducing words not supplied to this notice. The gazette records the development as a matter deserving careful attention in the public interest.
